messages:
maria_sales: Heads-up — customer call in 30m. POC ask: very spiky traffic (brief bursts up to 10k RPS), steady-state ~120 RPS, p95 latency goal ~120ms for chat completions. They want reserved capacity + autoscale and asked if HIPAA will block hosted API. tagging ops/security for clearance.
jamal_se: What model and mean tokens per request? that drives GPU footprint a lot.
maria_sales: They want an efficient option: redwood-7b q8, approx 35 input + 85 output tokens average. willing to accept quantized weights.
oliver_oncall: Quick back-of-envelope: steady 120 RPS * 120 tokens ≈ 14.4k tokens/s. With q8 redwood-7b on A10G class machines, expect ~2 GPUs for minimal headroom with batching; recommend reserved pool 3-4 GPUs for safety. For 10k RPS short bursts you need autoscale headroom ~6-9 GPUs depending on burst length and batching. Suggest SOW: reserved=4, autoscale_max=8, autoscale_min=2, burst_credit_pool enabled.
sara_sre: HIPAA note: Hosted public API is a blocker for PHI unless we offer BAA + Private/Dedicated with customer-managed KMS or HSM. Questionnaire items to collect: data residency requirements, will any PHI leave customer VPC, and who will hold keys. If they accept Dedicated/Private + BAA we can proceed.
maria_sales: They prefer managed hosted API but will accept Dedicated for HIPAA. Need an ops preheat plan we can include in SOW to hit p95 day 1.
oliver_oncall: Preheat runbook (high level): 1) seed KV/prefix cache with representative keys 2) run synthetic steady warm traffic to populate batching pipelines (10-20m) 3) enable autoscale prewarm for Dedicated pools 4) apply throttling/graceful-shed policy for overload. Example preheat command:
```
# preheat example
redwoodctl preheat --model redwood-7b-q8 --concurrency 150 --duration 15m --warmup-keys warmup_keys.txt
```
Also recommend adding a header to warmup requests: `X-Preheat: true` to avoid audit noise and cold-path logic.
cynthia_ps: Pricing summary: reserved 4 GPUs monthly + overage hourly for autoscale bursts + per-token usage for hosted calls. Enterprise addon (SLA/BAA) adds surcharge. I'll put together a ballpark with ranges for 4/6/8 GPU reserved options by EOD. Also will include 'cost drivers' table: long sequences, cross-region fallback, KV cache misses, burst > credit.
jamal_se: Please ask them for sequence length percentiles. If p99 or p95 have long sequences (e.g., >512 tokens) GPU needs jump. We can offer a tracer endpoint to capture anonymized lengths without PHI.
maria_sales: I've requested an anonymized sample distribution. Meanwhile, can we propose a default autoscale policy for the SOW?
oliver_oncall: Default recommend: min_instances=2, target_utilization=65%, scale_up_step=1 instance, scale_down_cooldown=180s, burst_credit_seconds=1800 (configurable). Fallback chain to document: 1) AZ spare capacity, 2) regional fallback (higher latency), 3) model-fallback to smaller quant variant. Include canary window for new model rollouts.
sara_sre: Security checklist for SOW: 1) BAA required for PHI 2) Customer-managed KMS/HSM for keys 3) Audit log retention configurable (default 90d) 4) Recommend network peering/PrivateLink for Dedicated. If they insist on hosted API with PHI, that's a blocker.
maria_sales: I'll draft SOW: reserved 4 GPUs, autoscale to 8, preheat runbook, Dedicated/Private option + BAA checkbox. @cynthia_ps add pricing ranges, @jamal_se @oliver_oncall create kickoff ops checklist.
cynthia_ps: On it. Sharing draft pricing and the cost-driver table by EOD. Also adding notes on credits for burst minutes vs sustained autoscale.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled preheat job started by oliver_oncall at 2026-03-23T15:43:10Z — job/pc-preheat-4499432100 running.
jamal_se: thumbs up. once we get sample traces I'll run perf sims (short synthetic traces) to validate GPU counts and update SOW.
maria_sales: thanks team — 4pm PT sync with customer then update here. :thumbsup:
